Main.sentence: Vatican City , [b] [c] officially the Vatican City State ( ___E:Italian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_language)___ : Stato della Città del Vaticano ; [d] ___E:Latin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_language)___ : Status Civitatis Vaticanae ), [e] [f] often shortened as the Vatican , is a ___E:landlocked U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Landlocked_country)___ sovereign ___E:city-state U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/City-state)___ .

Ruled by the ___E:pope U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope)___ , it is an ___E:enclave U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enclave)___ within ___E:Rome U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rome)___ and serves as the administrative centre of the ___E:Catholic Church U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church)___ .

Vatican City is governed by the ___E:See U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Episcopal_see)___ of ___E:Rome U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diocese_of_Rome)___ , commonly known as the ___E:Holy See U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_See)___ , itself a ___E:sovereign entity under international law U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Legal_status_of_the_Holy_See)___ , which maintains ___E:its temporal power U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temporal_power_of_the_Holy_See)___ , governance, diplomacy, and spiritual independence.

Vatican is also used as a ___E:metonym U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metonym)___ for the Holy See, which is the central governing body of the Catholic Church and Vatican City, comprising the pope and the ___E:Roman Curia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Curia)___ .

The independent state of Vatican City came into existence in 1929 via the ___E:Lateran Treaty U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lateran_Treaty)___ between the Holy See and the ___E:Kingdom of Italy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Italy)___ , which spoke of it as a new creation,  not as a vestige of the much larger ___E:Papal States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_States)___ (756–1870), which had previously encompassed much of ___E:Central Italy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Italy)___ .

With an area of 49 hectares (121 acres) [g] and a population of about 882  in 2024, it is the ___E:smallest sovereign state in the world both by area U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_area)___ and ___E:by population U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_population)___ .
It is among the ___E:least populated capitals U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_national_capitals_by_population)___ in the world.

As governed by the Holy See, Vatican City State is an ___E:ecclesiastical U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecclesiastical_jurisdiction)___ or ___E:sacerdotal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacerdotal_state)___ - ___E:monarchical U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monarchy)___ state ruled by the pope, who is the ___E:bishop of Rome U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bishop_of_Rome)___ and head of the ___E:Catholic Church U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church)___ ; the highest state functionaries are all ___E:Catholic clergy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_orders_in_the_Catholic_Church)___ of various origins.

The Holy See dates to ___E:early Christianity U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Early_Christianity)___ and is the principal ___E:episcopal see U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Episcopal_see)___ of the Catholic Church, which in 2018 had about 1.329 billion baptized Catholics in the world, in the ___E:Latin Church U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_Church)___ and 23 ___E:Eastern Catholic Churches U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Catholic_Churches)___ .

After the ___E:Avignon Papacy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avignon_Papacy)___ (1309–1377) the popes have mainly resided at the ___E:Apostolic Palace U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apostolic_Palace)___ within what is now Vatican City, although at times residing instead in the ___E:Quirinal Palace U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quirinal_Palace)___ in Rome or elsewhere.

Vatican City contains religious and cultural sites such as ___E:St Peter's Basilica U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Peter%27s_Basilica)___ , the ___E:Sistine Chapel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sistine_Chapel)___ , the ___E:Vatican Apostolic Library U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vatican_Library)___ , and the ___E:Vatican Museums U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vatican_Museums)___ .
They feature some of the world's most famous paintings and sculptures.

The ___E:economy of Vatican City U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Economy_of_Vatican_City)___ is supported financially by ___E:donations from Catholic believers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter%27s_Pence)___ , by the sale of ___E:postage stamps U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Postage_stamp)___ and souvenirs, fees for admission to museums, and sales of publications.
Vatican City has no taxes, and items are duty-free.

The name Vatican City was first used in the ___E:Lateran Treaty U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lateran_Treaty)___ , signed on 11 February 1929, which established the modern city-state named after ___E:Vatican Hill U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vatican_Hill)___ , the geographic location of the state within the city of ___E:Rome U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rome)___ . "Vatican" itself is derived from the name of an ___E:Etruscan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Etruscan_civilization)___ settlement, Vatica or Vaticum , located in the general area the Romans called Ager Vaticanus , "Vatican territory".

The ___E:Italian-language U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_language)___ name of the city is Città del Vaticano or, more formally, Stato della Città del Vaticano , meaning 'State of Vatican City'.

Its ___E:Latin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin)___ name is Status Civitatis Vaticanae ;   this is used in official documents by the ___E:Holy See U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_See)___ , the Church and the ___E:pope U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope)___ .

The name "Vatican" was already in use in the time of the ___E:Roman Republic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Republic)___ for the Ager Vaticanus , a ___E:marshy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marsh)___ area on the west bank of the ___E:Tiber U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiber)___ across from the city of Rome, located between the ___E:Janiculum U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janiculum)___ , the ___E:Vatican Hill U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vatican_Hill)___ and ___E:Monte Mario U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monte_Mario)___ , down to the ___E:Aventine Hill U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aventine_Hill)___ and up to the confluence of the ___E:Cremera U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cremera)___ creek.

The toponym Ager Vaticanus is attested until the 1st century AD: afterwards, another toponym appeared, Vaticanus , denoting an area much more restricted: the Vatican Hill, today's ___E:St. Peter's Square U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Peter%27s_Square)___ , and possibly today's ___E:Via della Conciliazione U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Via_della_Conciliazione)___ .

Because of its vicinity to Rome's archenemy, the ___E:Etruscan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Etruscan_civilization)___ city of ___E:Veii U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veii)___ (another naming for the Ager Vaticanus was Ripa Veientana or Ripa Etrusca ), and for being subjected to the floods of the ___E:Tiber U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiber)___ , the Romans considered this originally uninhabited part of Rome dismal and ominous.

The particularly low quality of Vatican wine, even after the reclamation of the area, was commented on by the poet ___E:Martial U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martial)___ ( ___E:AD U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anno_Domini)___ 40 – c. AD 102 ).  ___E:Tacitus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tacitus)___ wrote that in AD 69, the ___E:Year of the Four Emperors U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Year_of_the_Four_Emperors)___ , when the northern army that brought ___E:Vitellius U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vitellius)___ to power arrived in Rome, "a large proportion camped in the unhealthy districts of the Vatican, which resulted in many deaths among the common soldiery; and the Tiber being close by, the inability of the ___E:Gauls U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gauls)___ and Germans to bear the heat and the consequent greed with which they drank from the stream weakened their bodies, which were already an easy prey to disease".

During the ___E:Roman Empire U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Empire)___ , many ___E:villas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villa)___ were constructed there, after ___E:Agrippina the Elder U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agrippina_the_Elder)___ (14 BC – 18 October AD 33) drained the area and laid out her gardens in the early-1st century AD. In AD 40 her son, the emperor ___E:Caligula U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caligula)___ , built in her gardens a circus for charioteers.

It was later completed by the emperor ___E:Nero U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nero)___ and named the Circus Gaii et Neronis ,  usually called, simply, the ___E:Circus of Nero U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circus_of_Nero)___ .

The ___E:Vatican obelisk U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vatican_obelisk)___ in St Peter's Square is the last visible remnant from the ___E:Circus of Nero U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circus_of_Nero)___ .

It was brought from ___E:Heliopolis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heliopolis_(Ancient_Egypt))___ in ___E:Roman Egypt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Egypt)___ by the emperor ___E:Caligula U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caligula)___ .
The obelisk originally stood at the centre of the spina ( ___E:median U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Median_strip)___ ) of the ___E:Roman circus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_circus)___ .

The circus became the site of martyrdom for many Christians after the ___E:Great Fire of Rome U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Fire_of_Rome)___ in AD 64. Tradition states that it was in this circus that ___E:Saint Peter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Peter)___ was ___E:crucified upside-down U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross_of_St._Peter)___ .

In 1586, the obelisk was moved to its current position by ___E:Pope Sixtus V U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Sixtus_V)___ , using a method devised by the Italian architect ___E:Domenico Fontana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domenico_Fontana)___ .
Opposite the circus was a cemetery separated by the ___E:Via Cornelia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Via_Cornelia)___ .

Funeral monuments, mausoleums, small tombs, and altars to pagan gods of all kinds of polytheistic religions, were constructed before the construction of the ___E:Constantinian Basilica of St. Peter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constantinian_Basilica_of_St._Peter)___ in the first half of the 4th century.

A shrine dedicated to the ___E:Phrygian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phrygians)___ goddess ___E:Cybele U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cybele)___ and her consort ___E:Attis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attis)___ remained active long after the ancient Basilica of St. Peter was built nearby.

Remains of this ancient ___E:necropolis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_necropoleis)___ were discovered during renovations by popes throughout the centuries, increasing in frequency during the ___E:Renaissance U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renaissance)___ until it was systematically excavated from 1939 to 1941 on the order of ___E:Pope Pius XII U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Pius_XII)___ .
The Constantinian basilica was built in 326 over what was believed to be the ___E:tomb of Saint Peter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Peter%27s_tomb)___ , buried in that cemetery.
From then on, the land mass became more populated in connection with activity at the basilica.
A palace was constructed nearby as early as the 5th century during the pontificate of ___E:Pope Symmachus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Symmachus)___ (reigned 498–514).

Popes gradually came to have a secular role as governors of regions near Rome. They ruled the ___E:Papal States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_States)___ , which covered a large portion of the ___E:Italian peninsula U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_peninsula)___ , for more than a thousand years until the mid-19th century, when all the territory belonging to the papacy was seized by the ___E:newly created U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_unification)___ ___E:Kingdom of Italy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Italy)___ .
For most of this time, the popes did not live at the Vatican.
The ___E:Lateran Palace U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lateran_Palace)___ , on the opposite side of Rome, was their habitual residence for about a thousand years.
From 1309 to 1377, they lived in ___E:Avignon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avignon)___ in France.
On their return to Rome, they chose to live at the Vatican.

They moved to the ___E:Quirinal Palace U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quirinal_Palace)___ in 1583, after work on it was completed under ___E:Pope Paul V U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Paul_V)___ (1605–1621).
In 1870, after the ___E:capture of Rome U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capture_of_Rome)___ , popes have lived in the Vatican.
Their prior residence at the Quirinal Palace was taken over by the ___E:King of Italy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_of_Italy)___ .

In 1870 the pope's holdings were left in an uncertain situation when ___E:Rome was annexed U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capture_of_Rome)___ by Italian forces, bringing to completion the ___E:Italian unification U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_unification)___ , after a nominal resistance by the papal forces.
Between 1861 and 1929, the status of the pope of Rome was referred to as the "Roman Question".
Italy made no attempt to interfere with the Holy See within the Vatican walls.
However, it confiscated church property in many places.
In 1871 the Quirinal Palace was confiscated by the ___E:king of Italy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_of_Italy)___ and became the royal palace.

Thereafter, the popes resided undisturbed within the Vatican walls, and certain papal ___E:prerogatives U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prerogative)___ were recognized by the ___E:Law of Guarantees U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law_of_Guarantees)___ , including the right to send and receive ambassadors.

The popes did not recognize the Italian king's right to rule in Rome, and they refused to leave the Vatican compound until the dispute was resolved in 1929. ___E:Pope Pius IX U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Pius_IX)___ (1846–1878), the last ruler of the Papal States, was referred to as a " ___E:prisoner in the Vatican U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prisoner_in_the_Vatican)___ ".
Forced to give up secular power, the popes focused on spiritual issues.

This situation was resolved on 11 February 1929, when the ___E:Lateran Treaty U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lateran_Treaty)___ between the Holy See and the Kingdom of Italy was signed by ___E:Prime Minister and Head of Government U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Italy)___ ___E:Benito Mussolini U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benito_Mussolini)___ on behalf of King ___E:Victor Emmanuel III U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Emmanuel_III)___ and by ___E:Cardinal Secretary of State U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Secretary_of_State)___ ___E:Pietro Gasparri U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pietro_Gasparri)___ for ___E:Pope Pius XI U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Pius_XI)___ .
The treaty, which was ratified  and took effect on 7 June 1929,  established the independent state of Vatican City and reaffirmed the special status of Catholic Christianity in Italy.

The Holy See, which governed the Vatican City, pursued a policy of neutrality during ___E:World War II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II)___ under the leadership of ___E:Pope Pius XII U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Pius_XII)___ . ___E:German U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nazi_Germany)___ troops occupied Rome after the September 1943 ___E:Armistice of Cassibile U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armistice_of_Cassibile)___ , with ___E:Allied U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allies_of_World_War_II)___ forces pushing them out in 1944. Both sides respected the Vatican City's status as ___E:neutral territory U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neutral_territory)___ .

One of the main diplomatic priorities of Pius XII was to prevent the bombing of Rome. A high level of sensitivity led him to protest even the dropping of pamphlets over Rome by the ___E:Royal Air Force U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Air_Force)___ , claiming that the few which landed within the Vatican City violated its neutrality.

The British government's policy towards the Vatican, as expressed in the minutes of a Cabinet meeting, was "that we should on no account molest the Vatican City, but that our action as regards the rest of Rome would depend upon how far the Italian government observed the rules of war".

After the United States entered into the war, US officials were against bombing the Vatican City, fearful of offending Catholic members of the American military, but said that "they could not stop the British from bombing Rome if the British so decided".
The US military even exempted Catholic servicemembers from air raids on Rome and other areas with a significant Catholic presence, unless they voluntarily agreed to participate.
Notably, with the exception of Rome, and presumably the possibility of the Vatican, no Catholic US servicemember refused a mission within German-held Italy.
On the other hand, the British insisted "they would bomb Rome whenever the needs of the war demanded".

In December 1942, the British envoy to the Holy See suggested that Rome be declared an ___E:open city U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_city)___ , a suggestion that the Holy See took more seriously than was probably meant by the envoy, who did not want Rome to be an open city. Mussolini rejected the suggestion when the Holy See put it to him. In connection with the ___E:Allied invasion of Sicily U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allied_invasion_of_Sicily)___ , 500 ___E:United States Army Air Forces U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army_Air_Forces)___ aircraft ___E:bombed Rome on 19 July 1943 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombing_of_Rome_in_World_War_II)___ , targeting Rome's railway hub in particular.
Approximately 1,500 people were killed, and Pius XII, who had been described in the previous month as "worried sick" about the possibility of Rome being bombed, toured the affected areas.
Another Allied bombing raid took place on 13 August 1943, after Mussolini had been ___E:ousted from power U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fall_of_the_Fascist_regime_in_Italy)___ .
The following day, the new Italian government declared Rome an open city, after consulting the Holy See on the wording of the declaration.

Pius XII refrained from creating ___E:cardinals U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_(Catholicism))___ during the war. By the end of World War II, there were several prominent vacancies: ___E:Cardinal Secretary of State U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_Secretary_of_State)___ , ___E:Camerlengo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camerlengo_of_the_Holy_Roman_Church)___ , ___E:Chancellor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chancellor_of_the_Holy_Roman_Church)___ , and Prefect for the ___E:Congregation for the Religious U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congregation_for_Institutes_of_Consecrated_Life_and_Societies_of_Apostolic_Life)___ among them.  Pius XII ___E:created 32 cardinals in early 1946 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinals_created_by_Pope_Pius_XII_in_1946)___ , having announced his intention to do so in his preceding Christmas message.

In 1970 the ___E:Pontifical Military Corps U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_in_Vatican_City)___ , except for the ___E:Swiss Guard U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swiss_Guard)___ , was disbanded by ___E:Paul VI U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Paul_VI)___ .
The ___E:Gendarmerie Corps U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corps_of_Gendarmerie_of_Vatican_City)___ was transformed into a civilian police and security force.

In 1984 a new ___E:concordat U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concordat)___ between the Holy See and Italy modified provisions of the earlier treaty, including the position of Catholic Christianity as the Italian state religion, a position given to it by a statute of the ___E:Kingdom of Sardinia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_of_Sardinia_(1720%E2%80%931861))___ of 1848.

In 1995 construction of a new guest house, ___E:Domus Sanctae Marthae U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domus_Sanctae_Marthae)___ , adjacent to ___E:St Peter's Basilica U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Peter%27s_Basilica)___ was criticized by Italian environmental groups, backed by Italian politicians.
They claimed the new building would block views of the Basilica from nearby Italian apartments.
For a short while the plans strained the relations between the Vatican and the Italian government.
The head of the Vatican's Department of Technical Services robustly rejected challenges to the Vatican State's right to build within its borders.
The territory of Vatican City is part of the Vatican Hill, and of the adjacent former Vatican Fields.

It is in this territory that ___E:St Peter's Basilica U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Peter%27s_Basilica)___ , the ___E:Apostolic Palace U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apostolic_Palace)___ , the ___E:Sistine Chapel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sistine_Chapel)___ , and museums were built, along with other buildings.

The area was part of the Roman rione of ___E:Borgo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borgo_(rione_of_Rome))___ until 1929. Being separated from Rome, on the west bank of the river Tiber, the area was an outcrop of Rome that was protected by being included within the walls of ___E:Leo IV U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_IV)___ (847–855), and later expanded by the current fortification walls, built under ___E:Paul III U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Paul_III)___ (1534–1549), ___E:Pius IV U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Pius_IV)___ (1559–1565), and ___E:Urban VIII U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Urban_VIII)___ (1623–1644).

When the ___E:Lateran Treaty U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lateran_Treaty)___ of 1929 that gave the state its form was being prepared, the boundaries of the proposed territory were influenced by the fact that much of it was all but enclosed by this loop. For some tracts of the frontier, there was no wall, but the line of certain buildings supplied part of the boundary, and for a small part of the frontier a modern wall was constructed.

The territory includes ___E:St Peter's Square U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Peter%27s_Square)___ , distinguished from the territory of ___E:Italy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy)___ only by a white line along the limit of the square, where it touches Piazza Pio XII. St.

Peter's Square is reached through the ___E:Via della Conciliazione U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Via_della_Conciliazione)___ which runs from close to the Tiber to St Peter's. This grand approach was constructed by ___E:Benito Mussolini U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benito_Mussolini)___ after the conclusion of the Lateran Treaty.
St Peter's Square is also partially encircled by the ___E:Ricciolo d'Italia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricciolo_d%27Italia)___ , a small strip of Italian territory.

According to the Lateran Treaty, certain ___E:properties of the Holy See U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Properties_of_the_Holy_See)___ that are located in Italian territory, most notably the ___E:Papal Palace of Castel Gandolfo U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papal_Palace_of_Castel_Gandolfo)___ and the ___E:major basilicas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_basilica)___ , enjoy extraterritorial status similar to that of foreign ___E:embassies U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diplomatic_mission)___ .
These properties, scattered all over Rome and Italy, house essential offices and institutions necessary to the character and mission of the Holy See.

Castel Gandolfo and the named basilicas are patrolled internally by ___E:police agents of Vatican City State U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corps_of_Gendarmerie_of_Vatican_City)___ and not by ___E:Italian police U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law_enforcement_in_Italy)___ .
According to the Lateran Treaty, St. Peter's Square, up to but not including the steps leading to the basilica, is normally patrolled by the Italian police.
There are no passport controls for visitors entering Vatican City from the surrounding Italian territory.

There is free public access to Saint Peter's Square and Basilica and, on the occasion of papal general audiences, to the hall in which they are held. For these audiences and for major ceremonies in Saint Peter's Basilica and Square, tickets free of charge must be obtained beforehand.
The ___E:Vatican Museums U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vatican_Museums)___ , incorporating the Sistine Chapel, usually charge an entrance fee. There is no general public access to the gardens.
Guided tours for small groups can be arranged to the gardens and excavations under ___E:the basilica U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basilica_of_Saint_Paul_Outside_the_Walls)___ .
Other Vatican locations are only open to individuals who have business to transact there.

Vatican City's climate is the same as Rome's: a ___E:temperate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temperate_climate)___ , ___E:Mediterranean climate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mediterranean_climate)___ Csa .
It has mild, rainy winters from October to mid-May, and hot, dry summers from May to September.
Some minor local features, principally mists and dews, are caused by the anomalous bulk of St Peter's Basilica, the elevation, the fountains, and the size of the large paved square.
The highest temperature ever recorded was 40.8 °C (105.4 °F) on 28 June 2022.

In July 2007 the Vatican accepted a proposal by two firms based respectively in ___E:San Francisco U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco)___ and ___E:Budapest U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Budapest)___ ,  to become the first ___E:carbon neutral U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbon_neutrality)___ state by offsetting its ___E:carbon dioxide emissions U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_carbon_dioxide_emissions)___ with the creation of a ___E:Vatican Climate Forest U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vatican_Climate_Forest)___ in Hungary,  as a purely symbolic gesture  to encourage ___E:Catholics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church)___ to do more to safeguard the planet.
Nothing came of the project.

In November 2008 the Vatican installed ___E:solar panels U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solar_panel)___ on the roof of the ___E:Paul VI Audience Hall U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_VI_Audience_Hall)___ .

Within the territory of the Vatican City are the ___E:Vatican Gardens U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gardens_of_Vatican_City)___ (Italian: Giardini Vaticani ),  which account for about half of the Vatican territory.

The state's foreign relations are entrusted to the Holy See's ___E:Secretariat of State U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretariat_of_State_(Holy_See))___ and diplomatic service.

Nevertheless, the pope has absolute power in the executive, legislative, and judicial branches over Vatican City,  and is thus the only ___E:absolute monarch U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Absolute_monarchy)___ in Europe.

Acting with three other cardinals chosen by lot every three days, one from each order of cardinals ( ___E:cardinal bishop U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_bishop)___ , ___E:cardinal priest U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_priest)___ , and ___E:cardinal deacon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinal_deacon)___ ), he in a sense performs during that period the functions of head of state of Vatican City. The Vatican has implemented several environmental initiatives aimed to reduce its ecological footprint.

Since 2008, the Vatican has expanded its solar energy systems, including the installation of photovoltaic panels at various locations such as the roof of the ___E:Paul VI Audience Hall U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_VI_Audience_Hall)___ .
The city-state has introduced 35 electric vehicle charging stations to promote the use of electric vehicles and intends to gradually replace State-owned cars with electric vehicles.
Well before the European Union's 2021 deadline, Vatican City successfully banned ___E:single-use plastics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-use_plastic)___ in 2019, reducing plastic waste.

The Vatican's waste management system has improved, achieving a recycling rate of 55 per cent for municipal solid waste, with a goal of reaching the EU standard of 70–75 per cent.  Energy-efficiency measures, such as installing ___E:LED lighting U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LED_lighting)___ in St Peter's Basilica and transitioning to digital document management, have been implemented to reduce energy consumption and paper use. These efforts reflect the Vatican's commitment to the vision of Pope Francis's encyclical Laudato si' and the Apostolic Exhortation Laudate Deum .

Vatican City has no formally enacted ___E:official language U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Official_language)___ , but, unlike the Holy See which most often uses ___E:Latin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin)___ for the authoritative version of its official documents, Vatican City uses only Italian in its legislation and official communications.

Unlike citizenship of other states, which is based either on jus sanguinis (birth from a citizen, even outside the state's territory) or on jus soli (birth within the territory of the state), citizenship of Vatican City is granted on jus officii , namely on the grounds of appointment to work in a certain capacity in the service of the Holy See. It usually ceases upon the cessation of the appointment.

Citizenship is extended to the spouse and children of a citizen, provided that they are living together in the city.  Some individuals are authorized to reside in the city but do not qualify or choose not to request citizenship.

Anyone who loses Vatican citizenship and does not possess other citizenship automatically becomes an ___E:Italian citizen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_citizenship)___ , as provided in the Lateran Treaty.

The Holy See, not being a country, issues only ___E:diplomatic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diplomatic_passport)___ and ___E:service U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Service_passport)___ passports, whereas Vatican City issues ___E:ordinary passports U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vatican_and_Holy_See_passports)___ for its citizens.

In statistics comparing countries in per capita or per area metrics, Vatican City is often an ___E:outlier U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outlier)___ – these stem from the state's small size and ecclesiastical function.
For example, as most of the roles which would confer citizenship are reserved for men, the gender ratio of Vatican City citizenship is several men per woman.

Further oddities are petty crimes against tourists, resulting in a very high per-capita crime rate,  and the city-state leading the world in per-capita wine consumption due to its ___E:sacramental use U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacraments_of_the_Catholic_Church)___ .
A jocular illustration of these anomalies is sometimes made by calculating a "popes per km 2 " statistic, which is greater than two because Vatican City is less than half a square kilometre in area.
